title: APRIL 13. That tundish has been on my mind for a long time. I looked it up and find it English and good old blunt English too. Damn the dean of studies and his funnel! What did he come here for to teach us his own language or to learn it from us. Damn him one way or the other!
html_source:
Recall from earlier when the Dean of studies called the “tundish” of the lamp a “funnel”,

—Is that called a tundish in Ireland? asked the dean. I never heard the word in my life

Stephen observes the irony that (Irish) Gaelic is Ireland’s authentic language and that an Englishman was unfamiliar with a word from “good old blunt English”, being informed of his error by an Irish native.
